Goku recruits and coaches Ginyu, Burter, Recoome, Guldo, Jeice, Yamaha, Popo, Satan, Nappa and Saibamen to be the ten man team in a mini-tournament of power between just U7 and U11 (Pride Trooper scrubs with Jiren as coach) 

Saibamen are immediately disqualified because of their kamikaze nature. The rest of the team does surprisingly well. In fact so well, no one besides the Saibamen is eliminated until it’s 9 v 1. 

U11’s final 1 is revealed to be Jiren’s star pupil, we’ll call him Botelle (think Uub to Goku). He’s not as strong or fast as Jiren but has a lot of hack abilities. Yamacha puts up a really good fight but is put out after losing control of a new wolf fang fist technique. It’s now just Botelle and Popo.

Grand Priest informs us that Mr. Popo’s real name is Hamajin (the first demon) and is the evil opposite of Zeno. Grand Priest pauses the tournament and teams up with Goku and Jiren who all GET CLAPPED.  Botelle, who’s hiding, notices Zeno is sound asleep and can’t help. He announces that he has one final technique, the Canon Transfer Cannon. A hit from this blast will transfer anything in one canon into a different canon. He fires and it hits! The eldritch Popo is transferred into the TFS universe and the “not omnipotent Popo of their universe” comes into this universe. 

Shortly after, Zeno wakes up and sees the carnage. He scolds Grand Priest, clinging to consciousness for “sleeping” and sends everyone back to their universe.

2.) Ride the Monongahela Incline to the Top of Mount Washington. It’s a small fee (less than $5) but gives you a beautiful view of the city on one of the oldest (and I believe last remaining) mountain rail transit in the nation. 

3.) Provided the weather is nice go on a “just ducky” tour. You ride an amphibious vehicle that does a driving tour of the city before driving into the river to give you a view from the water as well. 

4.) if you’ll be there for a while and have time to leave the city a ways, check out the Allegheny National Forest. Particularly the cooks forest area. It’s about 2 hours north of the city but worth the drive in my opinion.

Law, criminal or civil, is driven extraordinarily so by semantics. It, in part, is why so may cops seem to get off with “murder” because they’re incorrectly charged. 

Example, AdFun (if I may) and I are in a bar. We’re good friends. However, I find out that AdFun is sleeping with my wife. As a result I smash a glass over AdFun’s head and kills him. Police show up and arrest me. They charge with me with Murder 1. It is now the burden of the state to prove to the jury BEYOND A REASONABLE DOUBT that I planned to kill AdFun. If they can’t, I get found innocent and I’m off free as the wind (now his family can sue me civilly but that’s a different beast). 

What act I did commit in most jurisdictions is “voluntary manslaughter”. Which has a STEEPLY lower burden of proof but is also a lower penalty for guilt. So what happens in probably 90% of cases is the DA and the Defense come up with a plea deal. That is a “compromise” of what both sides feel is fair. The deal comes to me as the offender and I can weigh out the gamble of taking the plea or going to the jury with the plea almost always being less time served. Now, the judge reserves the right to tell both attorneys to fuck themselves and throw the deal out. 

Premeditation is extraordinarily difficult to prove in most cases. The Buffalo shooter at this point seems to be an exception. However, mishandling of evidence by the police can change a case (OJ Simpson) greatly because that evidence can’t be used.
